description: We are AstraGo, a multidisciplinary team of six innovators from Santiago del Estero, Argentina, representing our country through intelligent space engineering. Combining systems thinking, geospatial science, edge computing, and UX design, we turn complex aerospace challenges into functional prototypes. Using agile methodologies, we built an operational hardware-and-software ecosystem to standardize planetary analogue testing and empower future Moon and Mars missions.
summary:
The exploration of the Moon and Mars faces a critical challenge: the lack of standardized methods to validate technologies and habitats in equivalent terrestrial environments. AstraGo solves this through an open-source platform that calculates a Planetary Analogue Similarity Index (APSI) between Earth and extraterrestrial bodies. Its hybrid architecture combines a GIS-style mission control web interface and an edge-computing server on a Raspberry Pi 5, automatically processing biophysical, atmospheric, and topographic variables using data from NASA and international agencies.
What does it do? Offers a comprehensive 18-variable model for Mars and a focused 4-variable model for the lunar South Pole (ISRU).
How does it work? A web interface connected to a Raspberry Pi 5 backend that executes REST requests and real-time weighting algorithms.
What benefits does it have? Quantitative scientific rigor, elimination of blind testing, and operational portability in remote scientific field camps.
What technology stack does it use? Raspberry Pi 5, HTML5/JS, Microsoft Planetary Computer (Sentinel/DEM), ISRIC SoilGrids, Open-Meteo, and NASA POWER.
details:
AstraGo is an open-source platform designed to solve the critical terrestrial validation bottleneck in space exploration by calculating a Planetary Analogue Similarity Index (APSI).

How it works: A web interface connected to a hybrid edge-computing backend running on a Raspberry Pi 5 executes REST requests and real-time weighting algorithms. It features a comprehensive 11-variable model for Mars and a focalized 4-variable model for the lunar South Pole.

Data sources: We integrate NASA POWER for climate and solar irradiance, Microsoft Planetary Computer for DEM and Sentinel imagery, ISRIC SoilGrids for regolith properties, Open-Meteo, and Copernicus DEM.

Benefits & Impact: AstraGo eliminates subjective, blind field testing for rovers, habitats, and spacesuits, significantly reducing preparation costs and providing quantitative scientific rigor for remote research camps.

Tech Stack: Raspberry Pi 5, Python, HTML5/JS, Google Cloud Run, and multi-source geospatial APIs.

Creativity: We bridged edge-computing hardware autonomy with global satellite intelligence, translating complex multidimensional planetary datasets into an accessible, portable mission-control tool designed by a multidisciplinary team from Santiago del Estero, Argentina.
